subject: Commitment floor adjustment and remediation plan — Peregrine pilot
messages:
From: Amelia Torres <amelia@peregrine.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Keene <sarah@peregrine.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: temporary commitment-floor adjustment for Q1 pilot

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for a great demo last week — the team is excited to move the Peregrine pilot into a limited production lane starting January. As we scope the pilot we wanted to surface a regulatory and traffic-profile constraint on our side that affects the standard SLA anchoring you propose.

What we need: a temporary commitment-floor adjustment for the first 90 days of the pilot. Specifically, we propose:
- Uptime anchor reduced from 99.95% to 99.5% for Jan–Mar 2027 for the tenant used by the pilot.
- Monthly remedy (service credit) capped at $20k for that period (regardless of calculated percent).

Rationale: our vendor routing and traffic shaping during the pilot will produce concentrated bursts that inflate perceived unavailability risk; removing strict uptime exposure for a short runway lets us validate the integration without triggering large automatic credits. We can commit to providing hourly traffic slices and incident context for every day of the pilot.

Can your team accept a timeboxed exception like this, and if so what information do you need from our side to make it official? I attached a short traffic summary to give a sense of expected burstiness.

If helpful, we could schedule a 30-minute call with product and legal to walk through the proposal and a mutual action plan.

Thanks — Amelia
Amelia Torres
Head of Platform Partnerships, Peregrine Analytics
amelia@peregrine.ai | +1 415-555-0192

Attachment: peregrine-pilot-traffic-summary.pdf

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Torres <amelia@peregrine.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 11:01:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary commitment-floor adjustment for Q1 pilot

Amelia —

Appreciate the clear ask and the data. High-level response from Redwood: we are open to a narrowly-scoped, timeboxed exception for pilot tenants if we can agree on a short list of controls and reporting obligations. To move quickly, here are the conditions we'd need in a provisional exception:

1) 90-day pilot window (explicit start/end dates) and a one-time automatic reversion to standard SLA after the window.
2) Hourly traffic and error-rate slices (you mentioned these) — delivered in CSV or shared Drive link no later than 72 hours after an incident window.
3) Incident response commitments: your on-call and our on-call point of contact, plus agreed escalation times for Sev1/Sev2.
4) Cap on credits as you proposed (we can accept a $20k hard cap) but credits will still be calculated as a percentage of monthly invoice and then floored at the cap.
4a) We prefer to express the cap as a USD ceiling rather than a percentage to simplify invoicing.
5) Telemetry access: temporary read-only log export (S3 link or equivalent) for incident verification. If that is not possible, we will require signed attestations and sample logs.

I'll loop in Legal (Laura) to draft a short amendment to the standard SLA that covers the above and includes a mutual action plan. Ben and Marissa — could you pick a target date for a 30-minute joint call?

If you can confirm: pilot start date 2027-01-10 and ability to deliver hourly slices, I will fast-track the provisional-exception template and get it to you within 48 hours.

Thanks,
Rishi
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0137

Amelia / Rishi —

Thank you for the draft parameters. From a legal/compliance perspective, a few clarifications and required additions before I can sign off on an amendment:

• Definition: we need to explicitly define the pilot tenant IDs and the time window (start/end). The exception must not be a global change.
• Credit mechanics: credits will be calculated under our standard formula (monthly invoice * remedy percent) and then compared to the proposed USD ceiling; the lesser amount will be applied. Language must make that sequencing explicit.
• Evidence & audit: to qualify for remedial credit under the exception, Peregrine must provide the hourly slices, incident timelines, and either (a) read-only access to the log export for the incident window or (b) a signed attestation accompanied by a sampling of logs. The attestation template will be provided if you cannot provide exports.
• Security: if telemetry is provided we need to whitelist the access method (S3 presigned, transfer over customer-managed bucket, or via a signed temporary Redshift export). No persistent access will be granted.
• Termination/rollback: if we detect evidence of customer-side misconfiguration contributing >50% of the impact, remedial credits under the exception are void. We should include a clear triage and dispute-resolution SLA (owner, timeline).

I will prepare a 1-page amendment ("provisional exception" template) that captures these points — Rishi, I will attach it to the HubSpot deal and share a link. Amelia, once you confirm the tenant IDs and the pilot start date we will issue the amendment for signature (DocuSign). Expect a draft by EOD Wed.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
laura@redwood.com
